title: NeoPixel RGB Color Mixer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Mix red, green, and blue values from 0 to 255 on the robot's two NeoPixels, see the glow, and copy the matching np[0] = (r, g, b) line of MicroPython.

educational.topic: RGB color mixing on NeoPixel LEDs
learningObjectives: Choose R, G, and B values from 0 to 255 to produce a target color.
Write the matching np[0] = (r, g, b) and np.write() lines for one or both LEDs.
Scale RGB values for a brightness percentage and round down to whole numbers.
prerequisites: The Maker Pi RP2040 board layout (Chapter 2)

controls.label: Edit: LED 0 / LED 1 / Both
controls.purpose: Choose which NeoPixel the sliders change.

controls.label: Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, White, Orange, Off
controls.purpose: Load a row of the chapter's color table.

controls.label: Clear, Caution, Stop, Standby
controls.purpose: Load a status color: green, yellow, red, or blue.

equations: closest name = table color with the smallest RGB distance; Custom color if the distance is over 60
assumptions: Each channel is 0 to 255, as in the MicroPython neopixel module.
limitations: A screen cannot show how bright a real LED looks at full power.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Direct manipulation with live code generation
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Sliders and number boxes drive glowing LEDs, a swatch, a closest-name match, and a code box
keyQuestions: What color do full red and full green make?
Which line of code changes only the second LED?
What happens to each number when brightness drops to 20%?
commonMisconceptions: Red plus green light makes brown, as with paint.
Changing np[0] updates the LED without np.write().
Brightness is a separate setting inside the NeoPixel.
assessmentOpportunities: Make the chapter's yellow and report its values.
Report the code values for yellow at 20% brightness.
Write the code for a red LED 0 and a blue LED 1.
